'''Carlo Willem Joannes Beenakker''' (born 9 June 1960) is a professor at [[Leiden University]] and leader of the university's [[mesoscopic]] [[physics]] group, established in 1992.

==Education and career==
Born in [[Leiden]] as the son of physicists [[Jan Beenakker]] and Elena Manaresi,<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.nrcreader.nl/artikel/6319/ik-wil-zo-dicht-mogelijk-bij-onsterfelijkheid-komen|url-status=dead|archive-date=27 February 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150227102355/http://www.nrcreader.nl/artikel/6319/ik-wil-zo-dicht-mogelijk-bij-onsterfelijkheid-komen|title = Ik wil zo dicht mogelijk bij onsterfelijkheid komen|publisher = NRC Handelsblad|date=19 July 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.nwo-i.nl/wp-content/uploads/2011/12/fom-expres-december-2011-173448.pdf|url-status=dead|archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20250829182259/https://www.nwo-i.nl/wp-content/uploads/2011/12/fom-expres-december-2011-173448.pdf|archive-date=29 August 2025|title=Interview in FOM Expres|publisher=Institutes Organisation of NWO|date=December 2011|volume=24|number=4}}</ref> Beenakker graduated from Leiden University in 1982 and obtained his doctorate two years later.<ref name="cv">{{cite web|url=https://hoogleraren.universiteitleiden.nl/s/hoogleraren/item/2022|url-status=dead|archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20240731114508/https://hoogleraren.universiteitleiden.nl/s/hoogleraren/item/2022|archive-date=31 July 2024|title=Carlo Willem Joannes Beenakker|publisher=Leiden University}}</ref>

After the awarding of his doctorate, he then spent one year working in the United States of America as a fellow of the Niels Stensen Foundation<ref>{{cite web|url=https://ilorentz.org/beenakker/cv/NielsStensenFellowships.pdf |title=60 Years of Niels Stensen Fellowships |publisher=Niels Stensen Foundation}}</ref> before returning to the Netherlands as a member of the scientific staff of the [[Philips Natuurkundig Laboratorium|Philips Research Laboratories]] in Eindhoven. He joined the [[Lorentz Institute]] for theoretical physics at Leiden University in 1991.<ref name="cv"></ref>

== Work ==
His work in [[mesoscopic physics]] addresses fundamental physical problems that occur when a macroscopic object is miniaturized to dimensions on the nanoscale.<ref name="bio1">{{cite web|url=https://bitp.kiev.ua/en/doctors/beenakker|title=Bio at the Bogoliubov Institute}}</ref><ref name="bio2">{{cite web|url=https://www.nwo.nl/prof-dr-cwj-carlo-beenakker|title=Bio at the Netherlands Science Foundation}}</ref> Quantum mechanical effects then play a decisive role, as demonstrated in the [[quantum point contact]] (a narrow constriction with a quantized conductance). To understand the universal quantum mechanical properties of mesoscopic systems, Beenakker adapted methods from the theory of [[random matrices]], originally developed in the context of [[nuclear physics]].<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Guhr|first1=Thomas|last2=Muller-Groeling|first2=Axel|last3=Weidenmuller|first3=Hans|title=Random-matrix theories in quantum physics: common concepts|journal=Physics Reports|year=1998|volume=299|issue=4–6 |pages=189–425|doi=
10.1016/S0370-1573(97)00088-4|arxiv=cond-mat/9707301|bibcode=1998PhR...299..189G }}</ref> Discoveries by Beenakker and colleagues include the one-third suppression of [[shot noise]] in metallic conductors and specular [[Andreev reflection]] in [[graphene]].<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Blanter | first1=Ya.M. | last2=Buttiker |first2=M. | title=Shot noise in mesoscopic conductors| journal=Physics Reports|year=2000|volume=336| issue=1–2 |pages=1–166|doi=
10.1016/S0370-1573(99)00123-4| arxiv=cond-mat/9910158| bibcode=2000PhR...336....1B }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last1=Efetov | first1=D.K. |display-authors=etal | title=Specular interband Andreev reflections at van der Waals interfaces between graphene and NbSe2| journal=Nature Physics|year=2016|volume=12| issue=4 |pages=328–332|doi=
10.1038/nphys3583| arxiv=1505.04812 }}</ref>

== Recognition ==
In 1993, he shared the Royal/Shell prize for "the discovery and explanation of quantum effects in the [[electrical conduction]] in mesoscopic systems". He was elected a member of the [[Koninklijke Hollandsche Maatschappij der Wetenschappen|Royal Holland Society of Sciences and Humanities]] in 2001, and the [[Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences]] in 2002.<ref>{{cite web|author= |url=https://www.knaw.nl/leden/beenakker |title=Carlo Beenakker |publisher=Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences |date= |accessdate=4 December 2024}}</ref> He was awarded one of the Netherlands' most prestigious science awards, the [[Spinozapremie]], in 1999.<ref>{{cite web |author= |url=http://www.nwo.nl/en/research-and-results/programmes/spinoza+prize/spinoza+laureates/overview+by+year/1999 |title=NWO Spinoza Prize 1999 |publisher=Netherlands Organisation for Scientific Research |date=11 September 2014 |accessdate=30 January 2016 |archive-date=16 March 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160316005430/http://www.nwo.nl/en/research-and-results/programmes/spinoza+prize/spinoza+laureates/overview+by+year/1999 |url-status=dead }}</ref> In 2006 he was honored with the [[AkzoNobel]] Science Award "for his pioneering work in the field of [[nanoscience]]".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://ilorentz.org/beenakker/cv/AkzoNobel/akzoScienceaward2006_EN.pdf |title=Nanoscience pioneer receives Akzo Nobel Science Award |publisher=Azko Nobel Corporation |date=28 September 2006}}</ref> He was granted an honorary doctorate from the Bogolyubov Institute for Theoretical Physics of the National Academy of Sciences of Ukraine.<ref name="bio1"></ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.universiteitleiden.nl/en/news/2018/10/carlo-beenakker-receives-honorary-doctorate-in-kiev|title=Carlo Beenakker receives honorary doctorate in Kiev|date=5 October 2018 }}</ref> Beenakker is a [[Fellow of the American Association for the Advancement of Science]]<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.universiteitleiden.nl/en/news/2024/04/remarkable-achievement-leiden-professor-appointed-aaas-fellow|title=Leiden professor appointed AAAS Fellow|date=26 April 2024 }}</ref> and of the [[American Physical Society]]<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.universiteitleiden.nl/en/news/2020/09/two-leiden-aps-fellows|title=Aarts and Beenakker elected APS Fellow|date=29 September 2020 }}</ref> and a [[Knight of the Order of the Netherlands Lion]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.universiteitleiden.nl/nieuws/2015/04/koninklijke-onderscheidingen-voor-carlo-beenakker-en-ton-bakker|title=Royal decoration for Beenakker and Bakker|date=24 April 2015 |language=Dutch}}</ref>
